checks: Each bounded affine or convex integrand defines a finite signed measure on the parameter space. Zero continuous integrals imply the affine measures vanish. Nonnegative integrals against all continuous nonnegative functions imply the convex measures are positive by regularity. The conclusion for every Borel cell follows for each test without selecting a common set of parameter values.

The affine constant test gives equal mass in every cell. The two physical marginals of each marked restriction are supported in compact X even when the cell is Borel and its restriction support is not closed. Their convex inequalities have the exact ambient test class and orientation needed by the physical martingale lemma.

The common Borel graph recovers each prescribed marked restriction from its physical marginal. Marginal concentration implies the lifted product map lands in N times N almost surely and both marks lie in the same cell. Extending f by zero off the closed N gives a bounded Borel input test for the physical martingale.

The finite Borel partition from radius delta/2 balls has the required diameter bound. The sum of cell couplings has the fixed marked marginals. Weak compactness on N times N preserves them and sends the integral of continuous parameter distance to zero. The displacement tests pass first for continuous input tests, then for all bounded Borel tests by signed-measure uniqueness on N.

Disintegration gives the full physical row mean and a parameter that is constant almost surely within almost every row. Multiplying the affine equality by a continuous weight of either sign and conditional Jensen by a nonnegative continuous weight proves the localized tests. Zero common mass is immediate.

The marked exposed-face relation is compact by continuity of the finitely many support functions. A finite cover by bounded Lipschitz charts gives finite surface measure, and differentiability of each chart implies uniqueness of the outer unit normal since any supporting normal is perpendicular to its tangent hyperplane. The Lipschitz area bound transfers the chart-null exceptional set to surface-null. In dimension one the endpoints are regular and counting measure applies.

On each boundary, compactness and closedness of the unit-normal graph make the sets of points with a pair of normals at distance at least 1/m closed. This makes the regular locus Borel and the normal relatively continuous by uniqueness and compactness. The finite disjoint base labels and a constant extension off the regular locus give the common Borel graph. The surface measure and its absolutely continuous submeasures or other finite densities concentrate on this graph.

Disintegrating the preserved-normal coupling gives a row concentrated on the closed exposed-face relation at the input normal. The base barycenter gives the sum of alpha_q q, and taking the inner product of the continuous row mean with the fixed input normal gives the sum of alpha_q h_q(u) with the stated equality.
